summary: Interpreted the retained receipt for the restarts revision of the sweep (CheckRun c6015a9dcbe94734bfc7089fff19e5c1: completed, tests_passed, exit 0, 17 parsed observations, 0 parse errors). Indices 0-15 reproduce probes A-C; index 16 is the sweep summary with seeds=60, steps_per_seed=60, elections=466, ordinary proposals=452, conf_change_proposals=249, restarts=471, violations=0. Recorded as holds-only with the defect claim refuted narrowly, focused on what the restart event could most plausibly break: because each restart rebuilds a node from what an application would persist (hard state plus last applied ConfState) and the check compares that node's committed index against the maximum it had previously reported, a committed-index regression or a committed (index, term) contradiction should have surfaced had the rebuilt instance resumed from a different point; no such witness appeared, nor two leaders in one term, nor applied > committed. This also turns the earlier knowledge entry from read into exercised: storage really is the configuration source the rebuilt instance adopts, and it did so without a configuration-equivalence panic and without diverging from the cluster. Kept explicit: a rebuilt node can be caught up by the leader before the next between-events check, so an interruption in its own history may be invisible; the harness supplies the ConfState itself, so this tests adoption of a correct configuration rather than an application's diligence in recording one; storage faults are outside the event set since writes always succeed; and the sweep still records no liveness witness for states where committed-but-unapplied changes leave no voter able to campaign, while configuration events still only touch node 4 so demotion of an existing serving voter remains unexercised. Gap 984747de5ed94b4ea8f6977b2a92808f-gap-2 stays open on those two items; the next step is adding the liveness witness event and a demotion of an existing voter.
